moves.name: 90/90 hip switch
moves.primaryNames: Piriformis · Gluteus medius · Gluteus maximus · Iliopsoas
moves.secondaryNames: Obturator internus · Tensor fasciae latae · Adductor longus · External oblique
moves.how: Sit with one leg bent in front at a right angle and the other bent out to the side, both knees at ninety degrees. Sit tall, then rotate your knees over to the other side and settle. Move slowly and stop where you can still sit upright.

moves.name: Ankle rocker
moves.primaryNames: Soleus · Gastrocnemius · Tibialis posterior
moves.secondaryNames: Tibialis anterior · Flexor hallucis longus · Flexor digitorum longus
moves.how: Stand in a short split stance with your front foot flat and rock your front knee forward over your toes, heel glued down. Rock back and repeat, going a little further each time. Point the knee straight ahead, then slightly in and out to find the tight line.

moves.name: Belly breathing
moves.primaryNames: Diaphragm · Transversus abdominis
moves.secondaryNames: Internal oblique · External oblique · Transversus thoracis
moves.how: Lie on your back with one hand on your chest and one on your belly. Breathe in slowly through your nose so the lower hand rises and the upper one barely moves, then breathe out longer than you breathed in.

moves.name: Cat-cow
moves.primaryNames: Multifidus · Longissimus · Rectus abdominis · Iliocostalis
moves.secondaryNames: Spinalis · Transversus abdominis · Rhomboid major · Semispinalis
moves.how: On hands and knees, round your back to the ceiling and tuck your chin, then reverse: chest forward, tailbone up, eyes ahead. Move with your breath and let the movement travel along your whole spine rather than just the middle.

moves.name: Chin tuck
moves.primaryNames: Semispinalis · Sternocleidomastoid · Digastric
moves.secondaryNames: Sternohyoid · Omohyoid · Levator scapulae
moves.how: Sit or stand tall and glide your head straight back, as if making a double chin, without tipping it up or down. Hold a couple of seconds and release. A good one to do at a desk.

moves.name: Deep squat hold
moves.primaryNames: Soleus · Gluteus maximus · Adductor magnus · Adductor longus
moves.secondaryNames: Gastrocnemius · Rectus femoris · Vastus lateralis · Longissimus · Gracilis
moves.how: Squat as low as you comfortably can and stay there, elbows inside your knees, heels down if possible. Rock gently, look around, breathe. Hold a doorframe for support while you build up to it.

moves.name: Heel and toe walk
moves.primaryNames: Tibialis anterior · Gastrocnemius · Soleus · Extensor hallucis longus
moves.secondaryNames: Extensor digitorum longus · Fibularis longus · Flexor hallucis longus
moves.how: Walk twenty steps on your heels with your toes lifted, then turn around and walk twenty on your toes. A quick way to wake up both sides of the lower leg before a run or a walk.

moves.name: Shoulder pass-through
moves.primaryNames: Deltoid · Pectoralis major · Pectoralis minor · Infraspinatus
moves.secondaryNames: Trapezius · Rhomboid major · Subscapularis · Teres minor
moves.how: Hold a broomstick or band in front of you with a very wide grip and raise it overhead and behind you, arms straight, then back. Widen the grip until it's smooth — never force it through.

moves.name: Side-rib breathing
moves.primaryNames: Diaphragm · Transversus thoracis · Serratus anterior
moves.secondaryNames: Serratus posterior superior · Serratus posterior inferior · External oblique · Internal oblique
moves.how: Sit tall with your hands wrapped around your lower ribs. Breathe in and try to push your hands apart sideways rather than lifting your chest, then let the ribs settle on the way out.

moves.name: Thread the needle
moves.primaryNames: Rhomboid major · Rhomboid minor · Trapezius · Semispinalis
moves.secondaryNames: Infraspinatus · Teres minor · External oblique · Multifidus
moves.how: From hands and knees, slide one arm under your body and across, letting that shoulder and the side of your head rest on the floor. Reach the other arm forward or up. Slow, and equal time each side.

moves.name: Wall slide
moves.primaryNames: Serratus anterior · Trapezius · Rhomboid major · Infraspinatus
moves.secondaryNames: Deltoid · Rhomboid minor · Levator scapulae · Supraspinatus
moves.how: Stand with your back and arms against a wall, elbows bent like goalposts. Slide your arms up, keeping contact where you can, then back down. Where you lose contact is the honest answer about your shoulders today.

moves.name: World's greatest stretch
moves.primaryNames: Iliopsoas · Adductor longus · Biceps femoris · External oblique · Pectoralis major
moves.secondaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Soleus · Rectus femoris · Semispinalis · Deltoid · Internal oblique
moves.how: Step into a long lunge, put both hands inside the front foot, then rotate one arm up to the ceiling and follow it with your eyes. Come back down, straighten the front leg for a moment, and swap sides. Almost everything gets a turn.

moves.name: Adductor squeeze
moves.primaryNames: Adductor longus · Adductor magnus · Adductor brevis · Adductor minimus · Gracilis · Pectineus
moves.secondaryNames: Transversus abdominis
moves.how: Lie on your back with knees bent and a ball or cushion between them. Squeeze steadily for a few breaths, then release without letting the ball drop. Easy to set up anywhere and a good first step before the harder inner-thigh work.

moves.name: Back extension
moves.primaryNames: Iliocostalis · Longissimus · Spinalis · Multifidus
moves.secondaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Biceps femoris · Semitendinosus · Semimembranosus · Quadratus lumborum
moves.how: Face down on a bench or the floor, hands at your temples. Lift your chest until your body is in line — no further — hold, and lower. Lifting past straight arches the lower back without adding anything.

moves.name: Bear crawl
moves.primaryNames: Rectus abdominis · Transversus abdominis · Deltoid · Serratus anterior
moves.secondaryNames: Triceps brachii · Rectus femoris · Vastus lateralis · External oblique · Gluteus maximus
moves.how: From hands and knees, lift your knees an inch off the floor and crawl forward moving opposite hand and foot together. Keep your hips low and your back flat enough to balance something on it.

moves.name: Bench press
moves.primaryNames: Pectoralis major · Triceps brachii · Deltoid
moves.secondaryNames: Serratus anterior · Anconeus · Pectoralis minor
moves.how: Lie on a bench with your feet planted and your shoulder blades pulled down and together. Lower the bar to the middle of your chest with your elbows about 45 degrees from your sides, then press it back over your shoulders.
moves.caution: Use a rack or a spotter — never press a loaded bar over yourself alone.

moves.name: Bent-over row
moves.primaryNames: Latissimus dorsi · Rhomboid major · Rhomboid minor · Trapezius · Teres major
moves.secondaryNames: Biceps brachii · Brachialis · Iliocostalis · Longissimus · Biceps femoris
moves.how: Hinge forward until your torso is somewhere near 45 degrees, back flat, weight hanging. Row it to your belly by pulling your elbows past your ribs, then lower fully. Your torso stays where it started — no rowing yourself upright.

moves.name: Biceps curl
moves.primaryNames: Biceps brachii · Brachialis
moves.secondaryNames: Brachioradialis · Flexor carpi radialis · Supinator
moves.how: Stand with a weight in each hand, palms forward, elbows at your sides. Curl up without letting your elbows drift forward, then lower all the way until your arms are straight. Straight at the bottom is half the exercise.

moves.name: Bicycle crunch
moves.primaryNames: External oblique · Internal oblique · Rectus abdominis
moves.secondaryNames: Iliopsoas · Rectus femoris · Transversus abdominis
moves.how: On your back, bring one knee in and rotate your opposite shoulder toward it while the other leg reaches long. Switch sides in a steady rhythm. Slower is harder; racing turns it into a neck exercise.

moves.name: Bird dog
moves.primaryNames: Multifidus · Longissimus · Iliocostalis · Gluteus maximus
moves.secondaryNames: Transversus abdominis · External oblique · Deltoid · Spinalis
moves.how: On hands and knees, reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your torso. Hold a beat, then swap. Imagine a glass of water balanced on your lower back — the point is the stillness, not the reach.

moves.name: Bodyweight squat
moves.primaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Rectus femoris · Vastus lateralis · Vastus medialis · Vastus intermedius
moves.secondaryNames: Adductor magnus · Soleus · Rectus abdominis · Longissimus
moves.how: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, toes pointed slightly out. Sit down and back as if reaching for a low chair, keeping your heels planted and your chest tall, then push the floor away to stand. Go as deep as you can without your lower back rounding.

moves.name: Burpee
moves.primaryNames: Rectus femoris · Vastus lateralis · Gluteus maximus · Pectoralis major · Triceps brachii · Deltoid
moves.secondaryNames: Rectus abdominis · Gastrocnemius · Soleus · Biceps femoris
moves.how: From standing, drop your hands to the floor, jump your feet back into a plank, do a push-up if you like, jump the feet back in and stand or jump. Pick a pace you can hold for the whole set.

moves.name: Chin-up
moves.primaryNames: Biceps brachii · Latissimus dorsi · Brachialis · Teres major
moves.secondaryNames: Brachioradialis · Rhomboid major · Trapezius
moves.how: Same as a pull-up but with your palms facing you and hands about shoulder width. The turned-in grip brings the front of your arm in properly, which is why most people can do more of these than pull-ups.

moves.name: Clamshell
moves.primaryNames: Gluteus medius · Gluteus minimus · Piriformis
moves.secondaryNames: Obturator internus · Obturator externus · Gluteus maximus
moves.how: Lie on your side with knees bent and stacked, heels together. Keeping your feet touching, open the top knee like a hinge, then close it slowly. Your hips stay stacked — if you roll back to get more range, you've lost the exercise.

moves.name: Copenhagen plank
moves.primaryNames: Adductor longus · Adductor magnus · Adductor brevis · Gracilis · Pectineus
moves.secondaryNames: External oblique · Transversus abdominis · Gluteus medius
moves.how: Lie on your side with your top leg resting on a bench or chair and prop yourself on your forearm. Lift your hips so your body makes a line, squeezing the bench with the top leg. Start with the knee on the bench rather than the ankle.
moves.caution: Inner-thigh work is easy to overdo — build the hold time slowly.

moves.name: Crunch
moves.primaryNames: Rectus abdominis
moves.secondaryNames: External oblique · Internal oblique
moves.how: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your hands light at your ears. Curl your ribs toward your hips to lift your shoulder blades, pause, and lower. The movement is your spine rounding, not your neck pulling.

moves.name: Dead bug
moves.primaryNames: Rectus abdominis · Transversus abdominis
moves.secondaryNames: External oblique · Iliopsoas · Multifidus
moves.how: Lie on your back with your arms straight up and knees over your hips. Slowly lower one arm and the opposite leg toward the floor while keeping your lower back pressed down, then return. Go only as far as you can without your back lifting.

moves.name: Dead hang
moves.primaryNames: Flexor digitorum profundus · Flexor digitorum superficialis · Latissimus dorsi · Flexor carpi ulnaris
moves.secondaryNames: Trapezius · Teres major · Rhomboid major
moves.how: Hang from a bar with straight arms and let your shoulders relax up around your ears, then gently pull them down a touch so you're not fully slack. Hold as long as your grip lasts.

moves.name: Deadlift
moves.primaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Biceps femoris · Semitendinosus · Semimembranosus · Iliocostalis · Longissimus
moves.secondaryNames: Trapezius · Latissimus dorsi · Quadratus lumborum · Vastus lateralis · Flexor digitorum profundus
moves.how: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot, hinge down and take hold with a flat back and your shoulders just in front of the bar. Push the floor away and stand tall, keeping the bar brushing your legs the whole way. Lower it the same way you lifted it.
moves.caution: If your lower back rounds, the weight is too heavy — reset and lighten it.

moves.name: Diamond push-up
moves.primaryNames: Triceps brachii · Pectoralis major
moves.secondaryNames: Deltoid · Anconeus · Rectus abdominis
moves.how: Set your hands together under your chest so your thumbs and index fingers make a triangle. Lower with your elbows brushing past your ribs, then press. Harder on the back of the arm than a normal push-up, so drop the rep count.

moves.name: Dip
moves.primaryNames: Triceps brachii · Pectoralis major · Deltoid
moves.secondaryNames: Pectoralis minor · Anconeus · Rhomboid major
moves.how: Support yourself on parallel bars with your arms straight. Bend your elbows and lower until your upper arms are about level with the floor, then press back up. Lean forward slightly for more chest, stay upright for more triceps.
moves.caution: Stop at the depth where your shoulders still feel settled, not stretched.

moves.name: Face pull
moves.primaryNames: Infraspinatus · Teres minor · Deltoid · Rhomboid major
moves.secondaryNames: Trapezius · Rhomboid minor · Levator scapulae
moves.how: Anchor a band at about face height, hold both ends and pull them apart and back toward your forehead, elbows high. Finish with your hands beside your ears and your shoulder blades gathered. Light and slow beats heavy and yanked.

moves.name: Farmer carry
moves.primaryNames: Flexor digitorum profundus · Flexor digitorum superficialis · Flexor carpi ulnaris · Trapezius
moves.secondaryNames: External oblique · Quadratus lumborum · Gluteus medius · Levator scapulae · Longissimus
moves.how: Pick up something heavy in each hand and walk. Stand tall, shoulders back, ribs stacked over your hips, breathing steadily. Distance or time, not reps — put them down when your posture starts to go, not your grip.

moves.name: Front raise
moves.primaryNames: Deltoid · Pectoralis major
moves.secondaryNames: Biceps brachii · Coracobrachialis · Serratus anterior
moves.how: Hold a weight in front of your thighs and raise it straight out in front to about shoulder height with a soft elbow. Lower slowly. Keep your ribs down so your lower back doesn't do the lifting for you.

moves.name: Glute bridge
moves.primaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Biceps femoris · Semitendinosus · Semimembranosus
moves.secondaryNames: Rectus abdominis · Multifidus · Adductor magnus
moves.how: Lie on your back, knees bent, heels close to your bottom. Push through your heels and lift your hips until your body makes a straight line from knees to shoulders, then lower without resting. Squeeze at the top rather than arching your lower back.

moves.name: Goblet squat
moves.primaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Rectus femoris · Vastus lateralis · Vastus medialis · Vastus intermedius
moves.secondaryNames: Adductor magnus · Rectus abdominis · Trapezius · Longissimus
moves.how: Hold one weight against your chest with both hands, elbows tucked in. Squat down between your knees and stand back up. The weight in front is what lets most people sit deeper and stay upright than they can empty-handed.

moves.name: Good morning
moves.primaryNames: Biceps femoris · Semitendinosus · Semimembranosus · Iliocostalis · Longissimus
moves.secondaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Spinalis · Multifidus
moves.how: With a light bar on your upper back (or hands behind your head), push your hips back and hinge your chest toward the floor. Stop where your back would start to round and drive your hips forward to stand. Small range, big feeling.

moves.name: Hammer curl
moves.primaryNames: Brachioradialis · Brachialis · Biceps brachii
moves.secondaryNames: Extensor carpi radialis longus · Extensor carpi radialis brevis · Flexor carpi radialis
moves.how: Curl with your palms facing each other, thumbs up, as if holding two hammers. The turned grip shifts the work toward the muscle along the top of your forearm — usually you can go a little heavier than a normal curl.

moves.name: Hip thrust
moves.primaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Biceps femoris · Semitendinosus · Semimembranosus
moves.secondaryNames: Rectus abdominis · Vastus lateralis · Adductor magnus
moves.how: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and a weight across your hips. Drive through your heels until your torso is level with the floor, ribs down and chin tucked, then lower until your bottom nearly touches down.

moves.name: Hollow hold
moves.primaryNames: Rectus abdominis · Transversus abdominis · Iliopsoas
moves.secondaryNames: External oblique · Rectus femoris
moves.how: Lie on your back, press your lower back into the floor and lift your shoulders and legs a few inches. Keep the pressed-down lower back at all costs — lift your legs higher if it starts to arch.

moves.name: Incline push-up
moves.primaryNames: Pectoralis major · Triceps brachii · Deltoid
moves.secondaryNames: Serratus anterior · Rectus abdominis
moves.how: Put your hands on a counter, table or bench and walk your feet back into a straight line. Do a push-up from there. The higher the surface, the easier it gets — this is how to build to a full push-up without ever doing a bad one.

moves.name: Inverted row
moves.primaryNames: Latissimus dorsi · Rhomboid major · Rhomboid minor · Trapezius · Biceps brachii
moves.secondaryNames: Infraspinatus · Teres minor · Brachioradialis · Gluteus maximus
moves.how: Set a bar at hip height, lie underneath it and grab it with straight arms, heels on the floor. Keeping a plank from heels to head, pull your chest to the bar and lower under control. Walk your feet in to make it easier.

moves.name: Jump squat
moves.primaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Rectus femoris · Vastus lateralis · Vastus medialis · Vastus intermedius · Gastrocnemius · Soleus
moves.secondaryNames: Biceps femoris · Rectus abdominis
moves.how: Drop into a quick half squat and jump straight up, arms swinging back then forward. Land soft — toes first, knees bending — and flow straight into the next rep. Quality of the landing decides how many reps you should do.
moves.caution: Land softly; skip this one on hard floors if it feels jarring.

moves.name: Lateral band walk
moves.primaryNames: Gluteus medius · Gluteus minimus · Tensor fasciae latae
moves.secondaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Vastus lateralis
moves.how: Put a loop band around your legs just above the knees, stand in a quarter squat and step sideways, keeping tension on the band. Take steps that stay the same size in both directions; the trailing foot should never click into the leading one.

moves.name: Lateral raise
moves.primaryNames: Deltoid · Supraspinatus
moves.secondaryNames: Trapezius · Levator scapulae
moves.how: Stand holding a light weight in each hand, elbows slightly bent. Lift your arms out to the sides to about shoulder height, leading with the elbows, then lower slowly. Light weight and no swing is the whole exercise.

moves.name: Lying leg raise
moves.primaryNames: Rectus abdominis · Iliopsoas · Transversus abdominis
moves.secondaryNames: External oblique · Rectus femoris · Sartorius
moves.how: Lie flat with your hands under your hips. Keeping your legs fairly straight, lower them toward the floor and lift them back up without your lower back arching off. Bend the knees to make it manageable.

moves.name: Mountain climber
moves.primaryNames: Rectus abdominis · Iliopsoas · Transversus abdominis
moves.secondaryNames: Deltoid · Triceps brachii · External oblique · Rectus femoris
moves.how: From a push-up position, drive one knee toward your chest and swap, keeping your hips level and low. Start slow and controlled and speed up only while your hips stay still.

moves.name: Neck isometric
moves.primaryNames: Sternocleidomastoid · Platysma · Semispinalis
moves.secondaryNames: Levator scapulae · Trapezius · Sternohyoid
moves.how: Put your palm against your forehead and press your head gently into it without moving, for a slow count. Repeat on each side and the back of your head. Gentle pressure — this should never be a strain.
moves.caution: Keep the pressure light and stop if it makes you dizzy.

moves.name: Nordic hamstring curl
moves.primaryNames: Biceps femoris · Semitendinosus · Semimembranosus
moves.secondaryNames: Gastrocnemius · Gluteus maximus · Rectus abdominis
moves.how: Kneel with your ankles anchored under something solid, body in a straight line from knees to head. Lower yourself forward as slowly as you can, catch with your hands and push back up. Even a few inches of controlled lowering is real work.
moves.caution: Very demanding — start with a small range and a hand catch every rep.

moves.name: Overhead press
moves.primaryNames: Deltoid · Triceps brachii · Supraspinatus
moves.secondaryNames: Trapezius · Serratus anterior · Rectus abdominis · Longissimus
moves.how: Stand with the weight at shoulder height, elbows under your hands. Squeeze your glutes and ribs down, then press straight up, moving your head back out of the way and finishing with the weight over your ears. Lower under control.

moves.name: Overhead triceps extension
moves.primaryNames: Triceps brachii
moves.secondaryNames: Anconeus · Deltoid · Rectus abdominis
moves.how: Hold one weight overhead with both hands, elbows pointing forward. Lower it behind your head by bending only at the elbow, then press it back up. Keep your ribs down so your back doesn't arch to help.

moves.name: Pallof press
moves.primaryNames: External oblique · Internal oblique · Transversus abdominis
moves.secondaryNames: Rectus abdominis · Multifidus · Deltoid · Gluteus medius
moves.how: Stand side-on to an anchored band, hold it at your chest with both hands and press it straight out. The band wants to twist you — your job is to not let it. Hold the arms-out position for a couple of breaths each rep.

moves.name: Pike push-up
moves.primaryNames: Deltoid · Triceps brachii
moves.secondaryNames: Trapezius · Serratus anterior · Supraspinatus
moves.how: From a push-up position, walk your feet in and lift your hips so your body makes an upside-down V. Bend your elbows and lower the top of your head toward the floor, then press back up. The closer to vertical your torso, the more your shoulders do.

moves.name: Plank
moves.primaryNames: Rectus abdominis · Transversus abdominis · External oblique
moves.secondaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Deltoid · Serratus anterior · Multifidus
moves.how: Rest on your forearms and toes with your body in one straight line. Squeeze your glutes, tuck your ribs down and push the floor away with your forearms. If your hips are sagging or spiking, the set is over.

moves.name: Prone Y raise
moves.primaryNames: Trapezius · Rhomboid minor · Supraspinatus · Deltoid
moves.secondaryNames: Infraspinatus · Serratus posterior superior · Longissimus · Rhomboid major
moves.how: Lie face down with your arms out ahead in a Y, thumbs up. Lift them a few inches, hold, and lower slowly. No weight needed for a long time — it's the lower part of the big back muscle doing the work.

moves.name: Pull-up
moves.primaryNames: Latissimus dorsi · Biceps brachii · Teres major · Brachialis
moves.secondaryNames: Rhomboid major · Rhomboid minor · Trapezius · Brachioradialis · Rectus abdominis
moves.how: Hang from a bar with your palms facing away, hands a little wider than your shoulders. Pull your elbows down toward your ribs until your chin clears the bar, then lower all the way. Start each rep from a full hang rather than a half one.

moves.name: Push-up
moves.primaryNames: Pectoralis major · Triceps brachii · Deltoid
moves.secondaryNames: Serratus anterior · Rectus abdominis · Transversus abdominis · Anconeus
moves.how: Set your hands a bit wider than your shoulders and make a straight line from heels to head. Lower until your chest is a fist off the floor with elbows angled back, not flared out, then press away. Your hips move with your chest, not after it.

moves.name: Reverse curl
moves.primaryNames: Brachioradialis · Extensor carpi radialis longus · Extensor carpi radialis brevis · Extensor digitorum
moves.secondaryNames: Brachialis · Biceps brachii · Extensor carpi ulnaris
moves.how: Curl with your palms facing down and your knuckles leading. Keep the weight light — the back of the forearm is much weaker in this position, and that's exactly why the exercise exists.

moves.name: Reverse fly
moves.primaryNames: Deltoid · Rhomboid major · Rhomboid minor · Infraspinatus
moves.secondaryNames: Trapezius · Teres minor · Longissimus
moves.how: Hinge forward with a light weight in each hand hanging below your chest. Open your arms out to the sides like wings, squeezing your shoulder blades together, then lower. Soft elbows, no shrugging.

moves.name: Romanian deadlift
moves.primaryNames: Biceps femoris · Semitendinosus · Semimembranosus · Gluteus maximus
moves.secondaryNames: Longissimus · Iliocostalis · Trapezius · Latissimus dorsi
moves.how: Stand holding a weight in front of your thighs, knees softly bent. Push your hips straight back and let the weight slide down your legs until you feel a strong pull in the back of your thighs, then squeeze your glutes to stand. Your back stays flat the whole time — this is a hinge, not a bend.

moves.name: Russian twist
moves.primaryNames: External oblique · Internal oblique
moves.secondaryNames: Rectus abdominis · Transversus abdominis · Iliopsoas
moves.how: Sit leaning back with your knees bent and feet light on the floor. Rotate your shoulders side to side, letting your ribcage do the turning rather than just your arms. Add a weight once the rhythm is smooth.

moves.name: Scapular pull-up
moves.primaryNames: Latissimus dorsi · Trapezius · Rhomboid major · Rhomboid minor
moves.secondaryNames: Teres major · Levator scapulae · Serratus anterior
moves.how: Hang from a bar with straight arms and pull your shoulder blades down and together — your body rises an inch or two and your elbows stay locked. Hold a beat, then relax back into the hang. The missing first step of a good pull-up.

moves.name: Scapular push-up
moves.primaryNames: Serratus anterior · Rhomboid major · Rhomboid minor
moves.secondaryNames: Trapezius · Pectoralis minor · Deltoid · Serratus posterior superior
moves.how: Hold a push-up position with straight arms. Let your chest sink between your shoulder blades, then push the floor away so your upper back rounds up. Elbows stay locked — only the shoulder blades move.

moves.name: Seated calf raise
moves.primaryNames: Soleus
moves.secondaryNames: Gastrocnemius · Flexor hallucis longus · Flexor digitorum longus · Tibialis posterior
moves.how: Sit with your knees bent about square and a weight resting on your thighs, feet on the floor or a small block. Push through the balls of your feet to lift your heels, then lower slowly. The bent knee is what shifts the work to the deeper calf.

moves.name: Shoulder external rotation
moves.primaryNames: Infraspinatus · Teres minor
moves.secondaryNames: Deltoid · Supraspinatus · Rhomboid major
moves.how: Tuck your elbow against your side, bent to a right angle, and hold a band or light weight. Rotate your forearm outward like a gate opening, keeping the elbow pinned, then return slowly. Very light — this is a small muscle group.

moves.name: Shoulder internal rotation
moves.primaryNames: Subscapularis · Pectoralis major
moves.secondaryNames: Latissimus dorsi · Teres major · Deltoid
moves.how: Same setup as the external rotation but pulling the band across your body instead: elbow tucked, forearm sweeping in toward your belly. The deep front-of-shoulder muscle is the one working, even though you can't see it.

moves.name: Shrug
moves.primaryNames: Trapezius · Levator scapulae
moves.secondaryNames: Rhomboid major · Rhomboid minor · Flexor digitorum profundus · Flexor digitorum superficialis
moves.how: Stand holding a weight in each hand and lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears, pause, and lower them fully. No rolling — a circle at the top does nothing the straight lift doesn't already do.

moves.name: Side plank
moves.primaryNames: External oblique · Internal oblique · Quadratus lumborum
moves.secondaryNames: Gluteus medius · Transversus abdominis · Deltoid
moves.how: Lie on your side propped on one forearm, feet stacked or staggered. Lift your hips until your body is a straight line and hold, breathing normally. Drop to a knee version if your hips start dipping.

moves.name: Side-lying leg raise
moves.primaryNames: Gluteus medius · Gluteus minimus · Tensor fasciae latae
moves.secondaryNames: External oblique · Quadratus lumborum
moves.how: Lie on your side in a long straight line, bottom knee bent for balance if you like. Lift the top leg up and slightly behind you, lead with the heel, then lower it under control. Height matters less than keeping your hips from rolling.

moves.name: Single-arm row
moves.primaryNames: Latissimus dorsi · Teres major · Rhomboid major · Biceps brachii
moves.secondaryNames: External oblique · Quadratus lumborum · Trapezius · Brachioradialis
moves.how: Put one hand and the matching knee on a bench, the other foot on the floor, and let the weight hang. Pull it up along your side until your elbow passes your ribs, then lower it all the way down. Keep your shoulders level rather than twisting to finish.

moves.name: Single-leg glute bridge
moves.primaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Biceps femoris · Semitendinosus · Semimembranosus
moves.secondaryNames: Gluteus medius · Gluteus minimus · Rectus abdominis · External oblique
moves.how: Set up like a glute bridge but lift one foot off the floor, knee pulled toward your chest. Push through the planted heel and lift your hips, keeping them level — if one side drops, lower the range until it doesn't.

moves.name: Sliding leg curl
moves.primaryNames: Biceps femoris · Semitendinosus · Semimembranosus
moves.secondaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Gastrocnemius · Rectus abdominis
moves.how: Lie on your back with your heels on something that slides — a towel on a smooth floor works. Bridge your hips up, then straighten your legs away from you and pull them back in without letting your hips drop.

moves.name: Split squat
moves.primaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Rectus femoris · Vastus lateralis · Vastus medialis · Vastus intermedius
moves.secondaryNames: Gluteus medius · Adductor magnus · Iliopsoas · Soleus
moves.how: Take a long step forward and stay there — this is one leg's work, not a walk. Lower straight down until your back knee nearly touches, then drive up through the front heel. Most of your weight stays on the front leg the whole time.

moves.name: Standing calf raise
moves.primaryNames: Gastrocnemius · Soleus
moves.secondaryNames: Tibialis posterior · Fibularis longus · Fibularis brevis · Flexor hallucis longus
moves.how: Stand with the balls of your feet on a step and your heels free. Rise as high onto your toes as you can, pause, then lower until you feel a stretch under your calves. Slow at the bottom is where most of the value is.

moves.name: Standing hip-flexor march
moves.primaryNames: Iliopsoas · Rectus femoris · Sartorius
moves.secondaryNames: Rectus abdominis · Gluteus medius · Transversus abdominis
moves.how: Stand tall, loop a band under one foot or just use your own leg, and lift that knee above hip height. Hold for a beat at the top and lower slowly. Keep the standing side steady rather than leaning away from the working leg.

moves.name: Step-up
moves.primaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Rectus femoris · Vastus lateralis · Vastus medialis · Vastus intermedius
moves.secondaryNames: Gluteus medius · Soleus · Biceps femoris
moves.how: Put one whole foot on a solid box or low step, roughly knee height. Stand all the way up by pushing through that foot — resist the urge to bounce off the back leg — then lower yourself down under control instead of dropping.

moves.name: Suitcase carry
moves.primaryNames: Quadratus lumborum · External oblique · Internal oblique
moves.secondaryNames: Trapezius · Flexor digitorum profundus · Gluteus medius · Longissimus
moves.how: Carry a single heavy weight in one hand and walk without leaning. The side NOT holding the weight is doing the work. Walk the same distance on both sides.

moves.name: Superman hold
moves.primaryNames: Longissimus · Iliocostalis · Spinalis · Multifidus
moves.secondaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Trapezius · Rhomboid major · Deltoid
moves.how: Lie face down and lift your arms, chest and legs a few inches off the floor at once. Hold, reaching long in both directions, then rest. Look at the floor rather than forward.

moves.name: Tibialis raise
moves.primaryNames: Tibialis anterior · Extensor hallucis longus · Extensor digitorum longus
moves.secondaryNames: Fibularis tertius
moves.how: Stand with your back against a wall and your heels a step or two out from it. Keeping your heels down, pull your toes up toward your shins as far as they go, then lower slowly. The front of your shin should be burning within a dozen reps.

moves.name: Triceps kickback
moves.primaryNames: Triceps brachii · Anconeus
moves.secondaryNames: Deltoid · Longissimus
moves.how: Hinge forward with your upper arm pinned against your side and your elbow bent. Straighten your arm behind you, squeeze, then bend back slowly. The upper arm never moves — only the forearm.

moves.name: Walking lunge
moves.primaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Rectus femoris · Vastus lateralis · Vastus medialis · Vastus intermedius
moves.secondaryNames: Gluteus medius · Biceps femoris · Soleus · Gastrocnemius
moves.how: Step forward into a lunge, lower until both knees are bent about square, then push off the front foot and bring the back leg through into the next step. Keep your torso upright and take long enough steps that your front shin stays close to vertical.

moves.name: Wall sit
moves.primaryNames: Rectus femoris · Vastus lateralis · Vastus medialis · Vastus intermedius
moves.secondaryNames: Gluteus maximus · Rectus abdominis
moves.how: Slide your back down a wall until your thighs are about parallel to the floor and your knees sit over your ankles. Hold, breathing normally. The burn is the point; stop when your form starts sagging rather than when it starts hurting.

moves.name: Wrist curl
moves.primaryNames: Flexor carpi radialis · Flexor carpi ulnaris · Flexor digitorum superficialis · Palmaris longus
moves.secondaryNames: Flexor digitorum profundus · Flexor pollicis longus · Pronator teres
moves.how: Rest your forearms on your thighs, palms up, holding a light weight with your wrists just past your knees. Let the weight roll down to your fingers, then curl it back up. Small range, slow tempo.

moves.name: Wrist extension
moves.primaryNames: Extensor carpi radialis longus · Extensor carpi radialis brevis · Extensor carpi ulnaris · Extensor digitorum
moves.secondaryNames: Extensor digiti minimi · Extensor indicis · Extensor pollicis longus · Brachioradialis
moves.how: Same position as the wrist curl but palms down. Lift the back of your hand toward you, pause, and lower slowly. Go lighter than feels sensible — the back of the forearm is small.

moves.name: Bent-knee calf stretch
moves.primaryNames: Soleus
moves.secondaryNames: Gastrocnemius · Tibialis posterior · Flexor hallucis longus · Flexor digitorum longus
moves.how: Same wall position as the calf stretch, but bend the back knee while keeping the heel down. The stretch drops lower, closer to your ankle — that's the deeper calf muscle rather than the one you can see.

moves.name: Butterfly stretch
moves.primaryNames: Adductor longus · Adductor brevis · Adductor magnus · Gracilis · Pectineus
moves.secondaryNames: Adductor minimus · Iliopsoas
moves.how: Sit with the soles of your feet together and your knees falling out. Sit up tall on your sit bones and lean forward from the hips. Pressing your knees down with your hands adds intensity you often don't need.

moves.name: Calf stretch at a wall
moves.primaryNames: Gastrocnemius
moves.secondaryNames: Soleus · Tibialis posterior · Plantaris · Flexor hallucis longus
moves.how: Stand facing a wall, hands on it, one foot well back with the leg straight and the heel down. Lean in until you feel the stretch high in the calf. Keep the back foot pointing straight ahead.

moves.name: Child's pose
moves.primaryNames: Latissimus dorsi · Longissimus · Iliocostalis · Spinalis
moves.secondaryNames: Teres major · Multifidus · Gluteus maximus · Quadratus lumborum
moves.how: Kneel, sit back toward your heels and reach your arms long in front with your forehead down. Breathe into your back. Walk your hands to one side to bias one half of your back at a time.

moves.name: Cobra stretch
moves.primaryNames: Rectus abdominis · External oblique · Iliopsoas
moves.secondaryNames: Pectoralis major · Transversus abdominis · Internal oblique
moves.how: Lie face down, hands under your shoulders, and press your chest up while keeping your hips on the floor. Go only as far as feels easy across the front of your belly, with your shoulders down away from your ears.
moves.caution: Come down if you feel pinching in your lower back.

moves.name: Cross-body shoulder stretch
moves.primaryNames: Deltoid · Infraspinatus · Teres minor
moves.secondaryNames: Rhomboid major · Trapezius · Supraspinatus
moves.how: Bring one arm straight across your chest and use the other forearm to draw it in. Keep the shoulder you're stretching down rather than letting it ride up toward your ear.

moves.name: Doorway chest stretch
moves.primaryNames: Pectoralis major · Pectoralis minor
moves.secondaryNames: Deltoid · Coracobrachialis · Biceps brachii · Serratus anterior
moves.how: Put your forearm on a doorframe with your elbow about shoulder height and step through gently until you feel your chest open. Try it with the elbow higher and lower — each height catches a different part.

moves.name: Figure-four stretch
moves.primaryNames: Piriformis · Gluteus maximus · Gluteus medius · Gluteus minimus
moves.secondaryNames: Obturator internus · Obturator externus · Quadratus femoris · Gemellus superior · Gemellus inferior
moves.how: Lie on your back and cross one ankle over the opposite knee to make a figure four. Reach through and pull the underneath thigh toward your chest until you feel it deep in the crossed hip. Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.

moves.name: Front-of-neck stretch
moves.primaryNames: Sternocleidomastoid · Platysma · Sternohyoid · Omohyoid
moves.secondaryNames: Digastric · Pectoralis major
moves.how: Sit tall, draw your chin back, then tip your head gently back and slightly to one side so you feel a line down the front of your neck. Very small movement, very light.
moves.caution: Move slowly and skip it if it makes you light-headed.

moves.name: Hamstring stretch
moves.primaryNames: Biceps femoris · Semitendinosus · Semimembranosus
moves.secondaryNames: Gastrocnemius · Gluteus maximus · Longissimus
moves.how: Put one heel on a low step with the leg straight, toes up. Hinge forward from the hips with a flat back until you feel a pull behind the thigh, and breathe there. Rounding your back makes it feel like more and stretch less.

moves.name: Jaw release
moves.primaryNames: Masseter · Temporalis
moves.secondaryNames: Digastric · Platysma · Sternohyoid
moves.how: Let your jaw hang loose, rest your tongue on the roof of your mouth and massage the muscle at the corner of your jaw with two fingers in slow circles. Open and close gently a few times.

moves.name: Kneeling hip-flexor stretch
moves.primaryNames: Iliopsoas · Rectus femoris · Sartorius
moves.secondaryNames: Adductor longus · Pectineus · Tensor fasciae latae
moves.how: Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward. Tuck your tailbone under and glide your hips forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the kneeling hip. Squeeze that side's glute — it deepens the stretch without leaning further.

moves.name: Lat stretch
moves.primaryNames: Latissimus dorsi · Teres major
moves.secondaryNames: Triceps brachii · Quadratus lumborum · External oblique · Serratus anterior
moves.how: Hold a doorframe or bar at about head height with one hand, sit your hips back and away from it, and let your side lengthen. Turning your ribs slightly away from the hand deepens it.

moves.name: Lying twist
moves.primaryNames: External oblique · Internal oblique · Quadratus lumborum · Multifidus
moves.secondaryNames: Gluteus medius · Tensor fasciae latae · Pectoralis major · Longissimus
moves.how: Lie on your back, bring one knee across your body toward the floor and let it fall, arms out wide. Turn your head the other way if it's comfortable. Stay for several slow breaths per side.

moves.name: Neck rotation stretch
moves.primaryNames: Sternocleidomastoid · Semispinalis · Levator scapulae
moves.secondaryNames: Trapezius · Platysma · Digastric · Omohyoid
moves.how: Turn your head slowly to look over one shoulder, stop where it gets firm and breathe for a few seconds, then come back and go the other way. Keep your shoulders square to the front.

moves.name: Overhead triceps stretch
moves.primaryNames: Triceps brachii
moves.secondaryNames: Latissimus dorsi · Teres major · Deltoid · Anconeus
moves.how: Reach one arm overhead, bend the elbow so your hand drops behind your head, and use the other hand to ease the elbow back. Keep your ribs down so the stretch stays in the arm.

moves.name: Pigeon stretch
moves.primaryNames: Piriformis · Gluteus maximus · Gluteus medius
moves.secondaryNames: Obturator externus · Quadratus femoris · Iliopsoas · Tensor fasciae latae
moves.how: From hands and knees, bring one shin forward across your body and stretch the other leg straight back. Stay tall on your hands, or fold down over the front shin. Put a cushion under the front hip if it hovers.
moves.caution: Ease off if it pinches at the front of the bent knee.

moves.name: Seated spinal twist
moves.primaryNames: External oblique · Internal oblique · Multifidus · Gluteus maximus
moves.secondaryNames: Quadratus lumborum · Longissimus · Piriformis · Semispinalis
moves.how: Sit with one leg crossed over the other, plant the top foot flat and turn your chest toward that knee, using your arm as a lever. Sit tall first, then twist — height before rotation.

moves.name: Shin stretch
moves.primaryNames: Tibialis anterior · Extensor hallucis longus · Extensor digitorum longus
moves.secondaryNames: Fibularis tertius · Extensor carpi radialis longus
moves.how: Kneel with the tops of your feet flat on the floor and sit back gently on your heels. You'll feel the fronts of your shins and ankles. Put a rolled towel under your ankles if it's too much at first.

moves.name: Side lunge stretch
moves.primaryNames: Adductor longus · Adductor magnus · Adductor brevis · Gracilis · Adductor minimus
moves.secondaryNames: Pectineus · Biceps femoris · Semimembranosus · Semitendinosus
moves.how: Stand wide, bend one knee and shift your weight over it, keeping the other leg straight with its toes up. You'll feel the inside of the straight leg. Rock slowly side to side rather than holding rigidly still.

moves.name: Standing forward fold
moves.primaryNames: Biceps femoris · Semitendinosus · Semimembranosus · Gastrocnemius
moves.secondaryNames: Longissimus · Iliocostalis · Soleus · Gluteus maximus
moves.how: Stand with your feet hip width, soften your knees and fold forward, letting your head hang heavy. Hold your elbows and sway gently. Bend the knees as much as you need — the point is the back of the legs, not touching the floor.

moves.name: Standing quad stretch
moves.primaryNames: Rectus femoris · Vastus lateralis · Vastus medialis · Vastus intermedius
moves.secondaryNames: Iliopsoas · Sartorius · Tibialis anterior
moves.how: Stand tall, hold one ankle behind you and draw your heel toward your bottom with your knees side by side. Tuck your tailbone under to feel it higher up the thigh. Hold a wall if balance is the limiting factor.

moves.name: Standing side bend
moves.primaryNames: Quadratus lumborum · External oblique · Latissimus dorsi
moves.secondaryNames: Internal oblique · Iliocostalis · Serratus anterior
moves.how: Stand tall, reach one arm overhead and lean away from it, keeping both feet planted and hips level. Reach long rather than folding over — you should feel a line down your whole side.

moves.name: Toe and arch stretch
moves.primaryNames: Flexor hallucis longus · Flexor digitorum longus · Soleus
moves.secondaryNames: Tibialis posterior · Gastrocnemius · Fibularis brevis
moves.how: Kneel with your toes tucked under so the balls of your feet take your weight, and sit back slowly. Strong sensation under the foot and in the toes — go gently and build the time up.

moves.name: Upper trap stretch
moves.primaryNames: Trapezius · Levator scapulae
moves.secondaryNames: Sternocleidomastoid · Semispinalis · Rhomboid minor
moves.how: Sit tall, hold the side of your chair with one hand and tip your head away from it, using the other hand for gentle weight. Breathe out into the stretch and stop well short of anything sharp.

moves.name: Wrist extensor stretch
moves.primaryNames: Extensor carpi radialis longus · Extensor carpi radialis brevis · Extensor digitorum · Extensor carpi ulnaris
moves.secondaryNames: Extensor digiti minimi · Supinator · Brachioradialis · Extensor pollicis longus
moves.how: Straighten one arm in front, palm down, and gently press the back of the hand down and toward you. Keep the elbow straight and the pressure light — this side is more sensitive than it looks.

moves.name: Wrist flexor stretch
moves.primaryNames: Flexor carpi radialis · Flexor carpi ulnaris · Flexor digitorum superficialis · Palmaris longus
moves.secondaryNames: Flexor digitorum profundus · Flexor pollicis longus · Pronator teres · Biceps brachii
moves.how: Straighten one arm in front, palm up, and gently pull the fingers back toward you with the other hand. Straight elbow makes the difference — bent, you'll barely feel it.
